title: Independent reciprocal-root order is recursively enumerable complete

decision_problem.input: integer polynomial Q in finitely many variables
decision_problem.quantifier: exists independently chosen positive integers n_1,...,n_k

completed_claims: The stated arithmetic problem is recursively enumerable complete.
Undecidability persists for some fixed finite number K of count variables and fixed finite polynomial degree bound D; no optimized K,D are asserted.
No total input-computable one-witness count bound defined on NO inputs also exists for this unrestricted problem.
No sound complete effectively checkable finite NO certificate system exists for all its NO instances.

mechanism.analytic_coordinate: f(t)=A(exp(-log(2)/t)); derivative tends to a=1/log(2) with O(t^-2) error
mechanism.successor: 5/4 < f(s)-f(t) < 7/4 iff s=t+1 for positive integer indices
mechanism.integer_variables: v_i=n_i-t, recovered up to a controlled small error by V_i=(f(n_i)-f(t))/(f(t+1)-f(t))
mechanism.single_inequality: An integer polynomial is obtained from one sum-of-squares penalty inequality by clearing denominators positive on the root domain.
false_witness_controls: negative v_i are permitted and covered by the oriented-integral bound
the polynomial value differs from the integer P(v) by less than 1/16
all input coefficients remain integers; log(2) is used only in the proof
mechanism.proof_outputs: Effective many-one reduction and finite witness existence, not an executed Diophantine solver.
